proof_summary: For the candidate shift, the binomial expansion shows all nonconstant terms are divisible by the modulus: when \(p^2\mid n\), taking \(T=n/p\) makes the linear term a multiple of \(n\) and every higher term contains enough powers of \(T\), while the shift \(n\) always works. For any period \(T\), testing shifts at \(0\) and \(1\) gives \(n\mid T^p\) and \(n\mid pTU\), where \(U\equiv1\) modulo every prime divisor forced into \(T\); hence \(\gcd(n,U)=1\) and \(n\mid pT\), from which prime-divisibility arguments yield the corresponding sharp lower bound on \(T\).
